wu: Students play 'Two Truths and a Resolution': each shares two past resolutions and one new one for the class to guess which is the new one using 'Will you...?' questions.
wuAlt: Students write three resolutions on slips of paper; teacher collects and reads aloud for class to guess the writer
Students interview a partner about their resolutions using 'How will you...?' and report back to the class
pres: Teacher displays a formal email template on the board with blanks for subject, greeting, request, closing; models filling it for a 'requesting a holiday extension' scenario; checks understanding with 'What do we say in a formal email?' questions.
presAlt: Teacher uses a real email from a local company (with sensitive info removed) to highlight formal phrases
Teacher roleplays a phone call followed by an email to show the connection between spoken and written requests
prac: Students complete a gap-fill exercise with formal email phrases (e.g., 'I am writing to...', 'Could you please...', 'Thank you for your consideration'); then rewrite an informal email into a formal one in pairs.
pracAlt: Students match request phrases to email parts (greeting, body, closing) in a cut-and-paste activity
Students play 'Email Bingo' with formal phrases they mark off when heard in a teacher dictation
ls: Students listen to two model emails (one formal request, one informal) and tick differences in a T-chart; then listen again to note specific request phrases.
re: Students play 'Simon Says' with action verbs related to email tasks (e.g., 'Simon says attach the document', 'Simon says send the email') to refocus after the break.
prod: Students write a formal email to a manager requesting time off for the New Year, using a checklist for structure and polite language; then swap drafts for peer feedback.
rw: Students read two short emails (one formal, one informal) about New Year plans and answer true/false questions about the register; then write a 50-word reply to one email using the formal frame.
st: Teacher shares a short story about 'A Resolution That Worked' and ends with the class saying 'Thank you for a great lesson!' as the goodbye routine.
g: Teams race to write a formal email line by line, passing the paper
Students roleplay a phone call and email exchange for a request
Students match phrases to email functions (e.g., 'Dear...' = greeting)
Students unscramble a formal email into correct order
Students act out a request for others to guess and write the email
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: write a follow-up email with a new request using 'Furthermore...'
Support / weaker learners: use a sentence frame template with options (e.g., 'I would like to request...')
hw: Draft a formal email to a teacher requesting a meeting about your progress
Write three resolutions and one strategy for each using 'I will...' and 'I am going to...'
Find a formal email online (e.g., a company) and list three formal phrases
tip: Model the email structure on the board step-by-step; Moroccan learners benefit from clear visual scaffolding for formal writing tasks.
